text:
Grass in summer is the color of envy, specifically the shade of green that turns yellow when you look at it too hard, because chlorophyll is just a jealous pigment trying to hide the sun’s secrets.

Speaking of secrets, my goldfish has abandoned hydrodynamics for astrophysics. She no longer swims; she orbits. She is currently charting the trajectory of a flake of dried blood as if it were the Andromeda Galaxy. She insists that the curved glass of her bowl is not a barrier, but a "lens of infinite possibility," and that her lack of legs is actually an aerodynamic advantage for space travel. She is convinced that if she swims fast enough in a counter-clockwise spiral, she will achieve escape velocity and launch herself into the ceiling fan, which she has designated as the nearest star. Do not correct her. She is busy calculating the gravitational pull of the heater, and she is very offended when you suggest that planets do not have gills.
